scope: Complete replacement of the fourteen existing game implementations, a dedicated DailyCoder-styled arcade, and ten new games. All original game URLs remain available through a static dynamic route.

research.method: Read official Google Play listings and inspected the Cricket Black, Archery Black, and All Black screenshot galleries. Android binaries were not installed or played. Store descriptions establish advertised mechanics; screenshots establish visible presentation. Improvements below are original design decisions, not claims about unobserved mechanics.

references.name: Cricket Black
references.observed: Side-on silhouette batting, tap-to-hit timing, target chases, and two-step bowling that sets pace and pitch.

references.name: Archery Black
references.observed: Limited arrows, a bow facing a target, tap-to-shoot timing, score attacks, target chases, and CPU competition. This is the Puran Software arrow reference; the unrelated arrow-exit puzzle is a separate extra game.

references.name: All Black
references.observed: Ten compact games: Archery, Cricket, Football, Basketball, Stone Throw, Bottle Shoot, Badminton, Bomber, Boxing, Runner.

references.name: Football Black
references.observed: Simple tap/swipe shooting focused on scoring goals.

references.name: Kanche
references.observed: Marble physics with challenge levels and multiplayer advertised.

references.name: Kanche 2
references.observed: Marble play, physical controls, and score competition advertised.

references.name: Blind Cricket Black
references.observed: An audio cue grows as the ball approaches; players time a tap at the loudest point.

references.name: 1 Brainy Shot
references.observed: One-shot bottle-clearing physics puzzles with designed levels.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: A readable bounce and a single committed action can carry an entire game.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Implemented original Boundary Cricket: animated delivery, anticipation, bat follow-through, timing feedback, visible shot flight, score attack, 24-ball chase, and batting/bowling match.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: Projectile travel time makes a simple tap an interesting prediction.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Implemented Arrow & Bow with a moving target sampled at arrow arrival, clear scoring rings, ten-arrow rounds, target chase, and CPU score duel.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: A clear target and quick retries make a strong short session.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Implemented Free Kick with direct aim controls, an animated reacting keeper, goal feedback, and ten-kick score/challenge modes.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: A readable arc makes learning from misses possible.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Implemented Pocket Hoops with hold/release power, arc animation, swish scoring, moving hoop positions, and directional feedback after misses.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: Aiming and trajectory can support authored puzzles, rather than only score attacks.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Reviewed as a future physics-puzzle candidate; not represented as shipped in this rebuild.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: Distinct targets and satisfying impacts matter more than decorative UI.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Target Rush uses original moving bullseyes, centre scoring, streak multipliers, hit effects, accuracy results, and keyboard access.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: Anticipation and return timing give a one-button sport depth.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Reviewed as a future sports candidate. Paddle Club is a separate original paddle game, not a badminton implementation.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: Moving projectiles and moving targets require leading the shot.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Reviewed for future development; no bombing game is claimed as shipped.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: A visible opening can create a fair timing challenge.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Reviewed for future development. Avoid hidden random failure; show a readable tell before an action window.

allBlackDesignReview.lesson: Deterministic hazards and immediate retries reward learning.
allBlackDesignReview.decision: Implemented Little Runner and an original eight-room platformer, One More Jump, with checkpoints, marked crumbling platforms, and predictable hazards.

architecture.isolation: ArcadeLayout imports only shared design tokens and its own scoped stylesheet and shell. It does not import the site authentication, Firebase, sync, ads, or search runtime. No other page imports the arcade. The hub has no player launcher; a player page loads engines through dynamic imports only after Play. Chess searches in a worker created only by the Chess player. Timers, listeners, animation frames, and workers belong to an abortable per-game session.
architecture.seo: Static, crawlable game links and unique rules; a title, description, canonical URL aligned with directory-format sitemap URLs, VideoGame and breadcrumb JSON-LD, and a local 1200×630 PNG social image per game. CollectionPage and ItemList schema for the hub. No remote game embeds or remote game media dependencies.
architecture.motion: Delta-time simulation; capped physics substeps for action games; optional synthesized audio; reduced decorative motion; automatic pause on tab hiding/window blur; pause-aware task queue; cleanup on page exit; cancelable computer thinking.
architecture.assets: Original code-generated SVG illustrations and PNG social cards. No images or code copied from the reference apps. Run npm run build:game-art after changing artwork generation or the catalog.
architecture.extension: Add catalog metadata, a same-slug player module exporting mount(session), and artwork. The glob creates the lazy entry automatically; static routes, hub cards, metadata, related games, and tests use the catalog.

verification.status: Verified: final full production build, all 26 game test groups, both emitted-resource audits and Pagefind indexing completed successfully.
verification.rules: 26 Node test groups pass, including Cricket variation, high-shot keeper saves, Football balance distributions, Basketball flight/floor physics, denser solvable arrows, favorites persistence, held touch input, paused fullscreen Escape, and Runner standing/ducking collisions.
verification.browser: All 24 polished players loaded from the final production preview at 390×844 with zero browser errors or container overflow. All players were checked at 320×740, 390×844, 844×390, 768×1024 and 1366×864 during the polish pass. Production lazy loading, favorites, related-game Back behavior, paused fullscreen focus/Escape and restart were verified. Additional game interactions are listed in polish.gameReview.
interactionChecks: A complete Hearts hand resolves thirteen tricks, preserves totals, and rotates passing in the next hand
A complete Spades hand resolves thirteen tricks and preserves partnership totals
All thirteen Yatzy categories complete and reach a result
Chess accepts e2–e4 and a legal worker reply
An entire nine-arrow introductory puzzle clears and advances to level two
Sudoku number entry, undo, and pencil notes work
Math Sprint accepts a computed answer and awards one score; initial focus stays on the answer input
Mobile block controls place a hard-dropped piece
Restarting a paused game clears inert state and restores the Pause label
Rendered dice pips fit within all five mobile dice faces
Chess pauses pending computer thinking, resumes with one legal reply, and Undo restores the previous position
verification.limits: This is browser smoke/play testing plus rule/property tests, not a physical-device lab or a Lighthouse score claim. Reference Android apps were researched via their official listings and screenshots. No online multiplayer or global leaderboards are claimed.
verification.buildNote: Existing social-image routes could not fetch their CDN font in this environment and completed using the system-font fallback. Game artwork and runtime assets are local; final build and audits passed.

polish.status: Complete and verified against the final production output.
sharedImprovements: Native desktop fullscreen includes the toolbar, pause/resume, restart, sound, dashboard navigation and exit. Phone/coarse-pointer browsers use a fixed expanded player without relying on fullscreen API support. Escape, focus trapping, focus return, safe areas and page scroll restoration are handled.
Held touch controls normalize keys, release held states on pause, and support deliberate repeat for block movement.
Game-to-game links replace the current game history entry. A game session stays one Back action from the games dashboard; direct game entries also receive a dashboard history anchor.
Favorite buttons on every dashboard card and game page persist locally, with a Favorites filter and storage failure handling.
Compact phone HUD/options, larger action controls, landscape side panels, and responsive canvas coordinates/cameras.
